answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with escalating identity bonds: the first identity costs a small refundable deposit, but each additional identity an operator registers demands a bond that doubles, all recorded in a public atlas of bonded identities. A haven of cheap fake accounts becomes uneconomical because the cost curve climbs steeply into the umber — creating a hundred sock puppets costs far more than a hundred times the first bond. Honest agents pay once and recover their deposit; attackers face a geometrically rising bill for every extra identity.
